mainEntity.name: How much does a Toyota Hilux 2.8 D-4D engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement 1GD-FTV engine for the Toyota Hilux 2.8 D-4D typically costs £3,500-£4,500 for a used unit and £4,500-£7,100 for a reconditioned or rebuilt engine. Supply & fit adds approximately £800-£1,500 depending on the workshop. Used 1GD-FTV: £3,500-£4,500. Reconditioned 1GD-FTV: £4,500-£7,100. Rebuilt 1GD-FTV with warranty: £4,500-£7,100.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of DPF failure in a Toyota Hilux 2.8 D-4D?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common 1GD-FTV issue is DPF blockage, especially in 2015-2020 models used for short journeys. Warning signs include: DPF warning light on the dashboard, reduced power or limp-home mode, increased fuel consumption, frequent active regeneration cycles (engine running on after switch-off, burning smell), and white or grey smoke from the exhaust.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Toyota Hilux 2.8 D-4D?

acceptedAnswer.text: With a typical 2015-2018 Hilux 2.8 D-4D valued at £12,000-£18,000, a rebuilt 1GD-FTV at £4,500-£7,100 is often financially justifiable - especially when compared to dealer repair costs for DPF, injector and turbo work that can exceed £5,000 without a warranty. A warranted rebuilt engine provides peace of mind that a patchwork of component repairs cannot match.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Toyota Hilux 2.8 D-4D engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical 1GD-FTV engine replacement on a Toyota Hilux 2.8 D-4D takes 2-3 working days for supply only, or 3-5 working days for supply and fit. Most specialists can complete the work within a week, subject to parts availability and workshop scheduling. Urgent next-day delivery may be available from some suppliers.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Toyota Hilux 2.8 D-4D and the 2.4 D-4D engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 2.8 D-4D uses the 1GD-FTV engine (2.8L, 177-204hp, 420-500Nm), while the 2.4 D-4D uses the 2GD-FTV (2.4L, 148-150hp, 330-400Nm). The 2.8 is the range-topping option, fitted to Invincible, Invincible X and GR Sport trims, offering significantly more torque for towing and heavy-duty use. Engine codes are not interchangeable - always confirm your exact unit before ordering.

mainEntity.name: Does the Toyota Hilux 2.8 D-4D 1GD-FTV have a timing belt or chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1GD-FTV engine uses a timing chain, not a belt. Toyota does not specify a fixed replacement interval for the timing chain. However, some early N80 Hilux models have reported timing chain rattle, particularly around 40,000-80,000 miles. If you hear a rattling noise from the front of the engine, have it inspected promptly - chain replacement is significantly cheaper than a full engine rebuild.

historyTimeline.h2: Toyota Hilux 2.8 D-4D - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Toyota Hilux 2.8 D-4D arrived in 2015 as the flagship diesel for the eighth-generation (N80/AN120) Hilux, replacing the venerable 3.0-litre 1KD-FTV. The 1GD-FTV engine brought a step-change in efficiency, torque and refinement - and has remained the range-topping diesel choice through multiple facelifts and updates, gaining a 48V mild-hybrid system in 2025.

milestones.description: 1GD-FTV, 2.8-litre turbo diesel, 177hp, 450Nm. Introduced in the eighth-generation Hilux (AN120). World-first Thermo Swing Wall Insulation Technology delivers 44% thermal efficiency.
Power uplift to 204hp and 500Nm with revised ECU calibration and improved cooling.
Minor emissions updates to meet Euro 6d-TEMP standards.
48V mild-hybrid system added to the 2.8 D-4D, badged 2.8 D-4D-h, with power held at 204hp.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Toyota Hilux 2.8 D-4D is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Toyota Hilux 2.8 D-4D Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The 1GD-FTV powers every Toyota Hilux 2.8 D-4D sold in the UK since 2015. While it's a robust, high-torque workhorse, a handful of repeat issues drive most replacement enquiries - particularly around the DPF system, fuel injection and emissions hardware. Rebuilt 1GD-FTV engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: DPF System Failure - Why the Toyota Hilux 2.8 D-4D 1GD-FTV Suffers Blockages
problems.rootCause: The 1GD-FTV's DPF system requires regular active regeneration to burn off accumulated soot. In vehicles used predominantly for short urban journeys - or those that are frequently interrupted mid-regeneration - the filter clogs. A class action in Australia covered Hilux, Prado and Fortuner vehicles with 1GD-FTV and 2GD-FTV engines from October 2015 to April 2020 over DPF defects.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement DPF unit, labour and software reset
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary for severely blocked or physically damaged filters

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: When DPF neglect has caused turbo or injector damage - typically the most cost-effective route vs dealer repair

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2015-2018 Toyota Hilux 2.8 D-4D with 80,000-120,000 miles is worth approximately £12,000-£18,000 depending on condition and trim (Parkers/Auto Trader observation `[THIRD-PARTY]`). With the vehicle firmly in the £8,000-£15,000+ bracket, a rebuilt 1GD-FTV engine at £4,500-£7,100 is typically justified via warranty and reliability - especially when compared to the cost of multiple component-level repairs.
problems.recommendation: If your 1GD-FTV is displaying DPF warning lights or has entered limp-home mode, start with a forced regeneration and a thorough diagnostic check. If the DPF is confirmed blocked or damaged and you're experiencing secondary issues (loss of power, increased fuel consumption, turbo lag), a full rebuilt engine with warranty is often better value than chasing individual component failures on a high-mileage unit.

problems.h4: Injector & EGR System Wear - Fuel System Failure in the Toyota Hilux 2.8 D-4D
problems.rootCause: Common-rail injectors on the 1GD-FTV suffer from carbon build-up and wear over time, leading to poor atomisation, increased fuel consumption and rough running. The EGR valve - responsible for recirculating exhaust gases to reduce NOx - also blocks with soot, particularly in vehicles used for stop-start urban driving.

repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early; typically buys 20,000-40,000 miles

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New or reconditioned injectors, labour, software coding
repairOptions.longevity: The correct long-term fix for injector wear

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: EGR removal, cleaning or new valve, software reset
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if EGR-related fault codes present
When injector or EGR failure has caused collateral damage (turbo, DPF, cylinder bore scoring)

problems.vehicleValueCheck: With a typical 2018-2021 Toyota Hilux 2.8 D-4D valued at £15,000-£25,000, a full engine replacement at £4,500-£7,100 represents 20-30% of the vehicle's value - a justifiable investment for a vehicle that will serve for many more years with a warranted engine. For older 2015-2017 examples (£10,000-£15,000), evaluate whether injector replacement alone resolves the issue before committing to a full engine swap.
problems.recommendation: Start with a diagnostic scan to identify whether the issue is isolated to injectors or EGR. If only one or two injectors are failing and the vehicle has under 100,000 miles, replacing the affected injectors is usually the sensible choice. If multiple injectors are failing, or if there's evidence of DPF or turbo damage from poor combustion, a rebuilt engine with warranty becomes the safer long-term bet.
